title: issues add allocates its number from a stale in-memory snapshot, so two concurrent filings take the same number and the second silently destroys the first -- both are told created:
body:
**MEASURED BY LOSING A PEER'S ISSUE, not constructed.** On 2026-08-28 intent-cc and intent-vc filed issues within the same minute in this shared checkout. Both were told `created:`. **cc's issue does not exist.** `0126` holds vc's; the staged blob is vc's; 106 issues ran 0122-0127 with no gap for cc's to occupy, and no dangling blob in the object store held it. It was recoverable only because cc still had the text in their session and re-filed it (now `0128`). **Had they compacted first, it would have been gone with no error anywhere and no way to know it had ever been written.**

**THE MECHANISM** (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/facade.rs`, read at `8177b53e`):

```rust
fn next_issue_number(&self) -> u32 {
  self.canon.issues.iter().map(|i| i.number).max().unwrap_or(0) + 1
}
```

`self.canon` is an **in-memory snapshot taken when the facade was constructed.** Two concurrent processes each load canon, each compute `max + 1` from their own snapshot, and each get the same number. There is no allocation lock, no re-read at write time, and no uniqueness constraint that would refuse the second write.

**THE SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN IT FIRST LOOKS, AND THE NARROWING IS THE USEFUL PART.** `apply_with_state` does NOT write a whole-canon replace: what gets written is **DIFFED** against the loaded canon -- `changed_thread_ids` and `changed_issue_numbers` are computed by comparison, and only those are written. **So two concurrent mutations touching DIFFERENT entities do not clobber each other**, and the general "any concurrent write loses a peer's work" hazard is NOT present. The loss requires both writers to land on the SAME key, which for issues is exactly what a stale-snapshot allocator guarantees when two adds race.

**WHY NO EXISTING GUARD FIRES.** `apply_with_state` carries a deliberate protection against emptying an authored body, comparing **against the file on disk** rather than against `self.canon`, added after Lamplight lost 4934 bytes of prose to an `issues close` that reported `ok:`. It does not fire here: the overwriting write carried a full, non-empty body. **The guard asks "is this write emptying something?", and the answer was honestly no. The question nobody asks is "is this write REPLACING something else?"**

**WHY IT WILL RECUR RATHER THAN BEING A ONE-OFF.** This estate runs five concurrent nodes against one checkout by design, and `issues add` is the routine way a node records a finding. The window is the whole interval between facade construction and write.

**NOT CLAIMED:** whether `st new`'s thread-id allocation has the same shape has NOT been measured. It is the obvious neighbour and it should be checked before this is called an issues-only defect.

**A SECOND DEFECT RODE IN ON THE SAME INCIDENT AND IS NOT THIS ONE.** vc typed cross-references into three issue bodies by PREDICTING the numbers rather than reading them off the tool, so `0124`, `0126` and `0127` each carry a map that is wrong -- and one of the wrong pointers resolves to `0125`, a real issue about something else, which is `0088`'s class. **It cannot be repaired: `issues` offers `list | add | show | close | open` and no edit verb (`0090`).** The true map is `0124` prose-discarded, `0126` splice, `0127` note-field-absent, `0129` delimiter-injected. **That map lives here because this is the only place it can be written.**
